articles.title: Can a volcano trigger the end of humanity? What would happen if Yellowstone supervolcano erupted now?
articles.summary: What if Yellowstone suddenly went from bubbling geysers and spectacular landscapes to the site of one of the largest volcanic eruptions in human history?
articles.body: What if Yellowstone suddenly went from bubbling geysers and spectacular landscapes to the site of one of the largest volcanic eruptions in human history?Yellowstone National Park in the United States of America may be famous for its geysers and wild beauty, but for some scientists and disaster thinkers, it’s also the setting for one of the biggest “what if?” scenarios out there. Imagine if, right now, Yellowstone’s calm was shattered by a massive supervolcano eruption. What would it really do to the park, the US, and the world? The short version: it would be a disaster on a scale most of us can barely picture.Before we divulge, it’s important to establish first that this is a hypothetical worst-case scenario, not a warning that Yellowstone is about to erupt.A recent report published by Phys.org, based on analysis by disaster researchers Ilan Kelman and Matthew Blackett for The Conversation, imagines what might happen if Yellowstone experienced a full-scale supereruption today. The scenario draws on volcanic research and previous disasters to create a possible “T-minus” timeline.In reality, the Yellowstone Volcano Observatory currently reports NORMAL volcanic alert status and a GREEN aviation colour code. Its September 2026 update recorded 61 located earthquakes in August, with the largest measuring magnitude 2.0, while ground deformation remained at background levels.So, what would happen if the nightmare scenario actually unfolded?Two months before: Yellowstone starts sending unusual signalsIf Yellowstone actually started ramping up toward eruption, we’d probably first get a warning sign a couple of months out. The scene: scientists start picking up swarms of earthquakes beneath the park. Not so weird, as Yellowstone has thousands of minor quakes every year, but these are different. They get stronger, clustered together, growing shallower. The ground starts bulging. Volcanic gases creep upward. Maybe geysers act odd, or new hot springs appear. Suddenly, emergency planners are looping in, updating evacuation blueprints, while volcanologists scramble to pin down what’s happening.Importantly, the US Geological Survey says that an earthquake swarm, ground deformation, or changing gas emissions individually do not mean an eruption is coming. Scientists would become much more concerned if several unusual signals appeared together and intensified rapidly.Two weeks before: evacuation beginsIf, a couple of weeks from doomsday, everything keeps escalating with stronger, shallower earthquakes, the land rising faster, officials would probably pull the plug for everyone living, working, or vacationing in the Yellowstone region. Imagine evacuating everyone within a 100-kilometer radius: almost 200,000 lives upended, plus thousands of tourists. Airspace is cordoned off as jets avoid the threat of ash.This would be a massive logistical challenge. Evacuations would involve finding shelter, food, water, electricity, transport, and medical care for large populations, while neighbouring regions and countries dealt with their own preparations.Eruption day: the first explosionsEruption day itself might not look like a Hollywood explosion — at least, not at first. Instead, the first violence could come when rising magma meets the park’s pressurized groundwater systems. Water rapidly turns into steam, blasting open the earth with steam, rocks, and mud. This is just the opening act. Soon after, as pressure drops, molten rock (magma) loaded with gas explodes upward and turns into fine ash and pumice. The ash cloud would shoot up: maybe 30 to 50 kilometers into the sky. That’s so high it dwarfs commercial air traffic altitudes.Within hours: pyroclastic flows and ashNow, a supereruption wouldn’t just be a local problem. Within hours, fast-moving pyroclastic flows (impossibly hot, suffocating clouds of rock, ash, and toxic gases) could sweep across huge swathes near Yellowstone, destroying everything in their path. Per the USGS, these flows would be concentrated mostly in Wyoming, Montana, and Idaho — all the areas closest to the supervolcano’s heart. Meanwhile, the eruption’s ash plume would catch high-altitude winds and start spreading.Three days later: ash becomes a national crisisA few days later, the ash blanket becomes a national crisis. A USGS model estimates that a supereruption shooting out 330 cubic kilometers of material would zip a deep, sometimes meter-thick, layer of ash across the Northern Rockies and pile up in cities like Billings, Salt Lake City, and Boise. Farther out (the Midwest, the coasts) would still get hit with centimeters or millimeters of ash, enough to foul up cars, clog engines, knock out power lines, and contaminate drinking water. Planes would be grounded across entire states, maybe more.Weeks later: food, transport and infrastructure come under pressureWeeks into the crisis, the country would start stumbling over new obstacles. Roads, runways, and rail routes would be choked by ash. No flights, no trucks, no trains running on time. Farmers would scramble to save crops that wither under the relentless, gritty blanket. Cattle would need clean water. Supply chains would struggle to move food, fuel, and medical supplies, while shortages could spread well beyond the areas directly covered by ash.Months later: the eruption fades, but the crisis doesn'tMonths on, the eruption itself winds down, but the chaos is far from over. Fine ash doesn’t stay put; winds pick it up, creating choking, dirty haze that makes it tough to breathe, especially for anyone with asthma or lung problems. Rain would transform ash deposits into gluey sludge, blocking storm drains and flooding streets. Even international trade starts feeling the pinch as America, a wheat and corn superpower, finds much of its harvest destroyed.Years later: global coolingBut probably the longest-lasting ripple comes from what the eruption would do to the world’s climate. The sulfur dioxide the volcano releases climbs high into the atmosphere, where it turns into sulfate aerosols. This stuff reflects sunlight, which means cooler temperatures around the globe. Not an “instant ice age,” but a real global chill: maybe about 1.5°C on average, according to some models. That doesn’t sound like much until you realize some areas (or farming seasons) might get whacked a lot harder, leading to worldwide food shortages and sharp price spikes. The planet would take years, or maybe decades, to fully bounce back.Would this end humanity?Honestly, no. The Yellowstone supereruption is a civilization-scale disaster, but it’s not a doomsday device. The USGS is clear: the odds of another huge caldera-forming blast in the next few millennia are vanishingly small, and Yellowstone isn’t on some fixed eruption schedule. If the volcano erupts again any time soon, a slower-moving lava flow is actually the more likely scenario, and that would be a challenge, but nothing approaching global catastrophe.The bottom line? While Hollywood loves the “supervolcano apocalypse,” what’s most probable (and what science shows) is less catastrophic. Yellowstone remains calm for now, and if that changes, we’ll have some warning. The site will stay under a microscope, and for good reason, but for now, the geysers and hot springs are a lot more dangerous to tourists snapping selfies than to humanity as a whole.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: Kalkaji gang-rape: Police probe if Aastha Kunj park was hunting ground of accused
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Police investigating the alleged rape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj park in south Delhi on Monday evening are trying to establish if the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Police investigating the alleged rape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj park in south Delhi on Monday evening are trying to establish if the three accused have been involved in similar incidents earlier that have gone unreported.They were clearly looking for a vulnerable target, say police sources, with Asif - armed with a pistol and a condom in pocket - taking the lead in entering the park, followed by the two brothers, Hemant Singh and Mukesh Singh. They then teamed up to unleash 40 minutes of terror on the hapless couple.Police sources said the girl and her friend were sitting on a bench around 7:15 pm when the three men allegedly approached them, posing as policemen in civvies.Having intimidated the two teenagers, they took the boy around 200m away and slapped and threatened him before taking the girl to a secluded, dark stretch of the park. That's where they took turns to allegedly rape her. The girl was threatened against disclosing the incident to anyone.Call detail records, CCTV footage place three accused near park at time of crimeShe was asked to leave the place immediately. By around 8pm, the men had left the spot, police said. According to the investigators, Hemant and Mukesh went out for dinner after that and returned home later. Asif seemed to be more cautious. Police got an early lead but couldn't find him either at the Okhla mandi or his house on Monday night.The girl returned to her friend and told him what had happened. The two left the park around 8:45pm. That's when the boy made a PCR call, which brought the cops to the park. The cops are now trying to establish how Asif had procured the pistol.They claim to have found "objectionable material", including videos, on Asif's phone, sources said. Some data was allegedly deleted from the phones of Hemant and Mukesh. These have been sent to Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) for retrieval.So far, the police have not come across any old complaints against the three. "We are checking whether someone may not have filed a complaint because of threats," a senior police officer said.The police are pursuing this angle because the three men would often hang around the park in the late hours. Hemant and Mukesh have allegedly changed their statements frequently during questioning. At one point, they claimed they were at home when the incident took place but gave a different account later. Their call detail records and CCTV footage, however, allegedly placed them near the park at the time.Sources said police are also investigating allegations that Hemant was removed from a gym he frequented following complaints of misbehaviour against him. The three have been sent to judicial custody for two days.DDA is facing a lot of flak for not having improved security in the park despite being alerted at least three times by the police since 2025. The police have pointed out that there were no CCTV cameras inside the park.Sources in DDA said their horticulture department had written multiple letters in the past one year to increase patrolling at the park. "Nine security guards are deployed in each shift at strategic locations, along with supervisory and patrolling arrangements. The lighting installations in the Aastha Kunj Park are functional and are inspected regularly. However, installing cameras at each spot won't be practical," a DDA official said.Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar, meanwhile, visited Aastha Kunj Park around 8.15pm Tuesday. He patrolled the park with other officers and reviewed security arrangements in and around the premises. articles.title: 9 dead after moving bus catches fire on Yamuna Expressway near Noida airport
articles.summary: NOIDA: Nine passengers were killed after a private bus travelling from Delhi to Mahoba caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway near Jewar late Wednesday
articles.body: NOIDA: Nine passengers were killed after a private bus travelling from Delhi to Mahoba caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway near Jewar late Wednesday night.Several other passengers sustained burn injuries and were rushed to Kailash Hospital in Jewar, officials said.The incident occurred around 11.30pm near kilometre 33 of the Yamuna Expressway, when the bus, operated by Raj Kalpana Travels, was travelling from Delhi towards Agra. The complainant, Sunil Kumar, a resident of Hamirpur, told police that around 30-35 passengers were travelling in the bus.According to the complaint, passengers began noticing a burning smell coming from the driver's cabin. They allegedly informed the driver and conductor about it, but the two did not stop the bus or inspect the suspected source of the smell. The complaint further alleged that the driver and conductor continued smoking inside the cabin and dismissed the passengers' concerns, saying that such a smell was common in the bus.A short while later, flames suddenly erupted near the driver's seat and rapidly spread through the vehicle. Passengers raised an alarm and repeatedly asked the driver to stop the bus, but the driver allegedly failed to act immediately.As the fire intensified, smoke filled the passenger compartment, leaving several people trapped inside. Sunil and some other passengers managed to escape by jumping out of the bus after it stopped. Several others, however, were unable to get out because of the flames and thick smoke.The injured passengers were taken to Kailash Hospital in Jewar for treatment. On reaching the hospital, the complainant was informed that doctors had declared nine people dead.The complaint also stated that passengers' bags, mobile phones and other belongings were destroyed in the fire. Luggage kept in the bus's luggage compartment and on its roof was also burnt.Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh each from the PM National Relief Fund for the next of kin of the nine deceased and Rs 50,000 for each injured person.Expressing grief over the incident, Modi said he was "distressed" by the loss of lives and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured.President Droupadi Murmu also expressed grief over the deaths and extended condolences to the families of the victims. Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath had earlier announced financial assistance of Rs 2 lakh each for the families of the deceased and Rs 50,000 each for the injured.Police have registered a case based on the complaint and initiated an investigation. The identities of the deceased and the exact cause of the fire are yet to be officially ascertained. articles.summary: US President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday, rolling out an elaborate military reception as the
articles.body: US President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday, rolling out an elaborate military reception as the Chinese leader began a three-day state visit to Washington.Xi and Chinese First Lady Peng Liyuan arrived at the Maryland airbase, where Trump and First Lady Melania Trump were waiting to receive them. The high-profile welcome featured a 100-foot-long red carpet, a salute battery, a 21-person honour cordon and colour teams carrying the US and Chinese flags.Two B-1 bombers also flew over the airbase as part of the welcome. The supersonic aircraft, a key component of the US military's long-range bomber fleet, are known for their distinctive loud roar during low-level flyovers.After a brief exchange with Trump and Melania, the Chinese couple walked down the red carpet before leaving the airbase in a motorcade. Trump and Melania returned to the White House aboard Marine One.The elaborate reception marks Xi's first trip to Washington since 2015 and comes as the two leaders prepare for talks on trade, tariffs, technology, artificial intelligence, military ties, Taiwan, Iran and the Russia-Ukraine war.Why the welcome mattersTrump's decision to personally receive Xi at the airport marks an unusually high-profile gesture towards a visiting foreign leader. According to the material provided, it was the first time since 1962 that a US president had welcomed a foreign leader at an airport.The reception also appears to reciprocate the ceremonial grandeur surrounding Trump's visit to China in May. Xi did not personally receive Trump when he arrived in Beijing, with Chinese vice-president Han Zheng welcoming him instead. Trump was nevertheless given a formal reception featuring a red carpet, military honour guard, military band and hundreds of Chinese youths carrying US and Chinese flags.Melania Trump had earlier said her husband decided to personally greet Xi because "they have a great relationship", adding that Xi was visiting US soil and should be welcomed "with the most respect".Follow live updates: Xi Jinping arrives in Washington as Trump gives rare airport welcome to kick off US state visitYou use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Residents of Sriniwaspuri Extension, where brothers Hemant Singh and Mukesh Singh- accused of raping a minor-lived, said they kept their distance from the two.The brothers were close, neighbours said, and would usually be seen together, usually exercising or lounging on the terrace."They would start a fight if anyone even stepped onto their part of the terrace," said a neighbour, who did not wish to be named, adding that Hemant claimed to be a lawyer and said even if someone complained against him, nothing would happen to him.Hemant and Mukesh, along with Asif, were arrested Tuesday for the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl in south Delhi's Aastha Kunj Park.Investigators said the two brothers were familiar with the park's layout and its dark spots as they used to play cricket there. This is where they met Asif three months ago, police said.Hemant's father, advocate J R Dhankar, told police that Mukesh is a BSc student and Hemant is a lawyer, a claim that cops are verifying. articles.title: A 1915 Rolls-Royce Silver Ghost spent 100 years with one Australian family; it emerged from storage for a 2026 auction
articles.summary: A 1915 Rolls-Royce 40/50 HP Silver Ghost Tourer spent about a century with one Australian family before emerging from long-term storage and appearing at
articles.body: A 1915 Rolls-Royce 40/50 HP Silver Ghost Tourer spent about a century with one Australian family before emerging from long-term storage and appearing at auction in 2026. Chassis 17CB, fitted with its original Barker tourer coachwork, was offered as Lot 40 at Gooding Christie’s 2026 Amelia Island Auctions with a pre-sale estimate of $350,000 to $450,000. The auction house highlighted the car's original engine, gearbox and coachwork, along with its unusually long documented ownership history.The Silver Ghost was not sold at the Amelia Island auction. The published auction results record the car as unsold, leaving its 2026 appearance as the latest chapter in the history of a Rolls-Royce that remained with the same Australian family from 1924 for roughly 100 years.The Silver Ghost retains its original engine and Barker coachworkChassis 17CB is a 1915 Rolls-Royce 40/50 HP Silver Ghost with a 7,428cc six-cylinder engine and four-speed gearbox. Gooding Christie’s identifies the engine and gearbox as original to the car. The Silver Ghost also retains its Barker-built open tourer body, numbered 4057. The car's originality is particularly notable because it remained in regular use in Australia rather than being preserved solely as a collector vehicle. Its body was modified during its working life to increase carrying capacity, but the original Barker coachwork remained with the chassis. The car also retains its original numbered engine and gearbox. When the engine was dismantled in the 1960s because the family was considering a rebuild, it was reportedly found to be in sufficiently good condition that a rebore was all that was required. The replacement engine blocks that had been obtained were subsequently sold.It arrived in Australia in 1915The car was completed at Rolls-Royce and went “off test” on August 5, 1915. Its records specify Barker open tourer coachwork, body number 4057, and equipment suitable for Australian roads. The car was exported to Australia through Kellow-Falkiner in Melbourne. Its original purchaser was Robert Alexander, a cattle breeder associated with the Hunter Valley in New South Wales. After Alexander acquired another new Rolls-Royce, 17CB was offered for sale in 1923. The car was subsequently bought by Robert C. Falconer. Historical records state that Falconer travelled to Sydney to purchase it, after which the Silver Ghost was registered to his wife at the family's estate in Claremont, Western Australia, in September 1924.The Falconer family used it across Western AustraliaThe Silver Ghost remained with the Falconer family for the next century. It travelled between the family's Perth home in Claremont and their rural properties and was used on journeys into remote parts of Western Australia. Its working life included trips to the Canning Stock Route, farms around the state and areas associated with the family's mining interests.During the Second World War, the family converted the car to run using a gas producer and charcoal. The Silver Ghost was also used to tow an agricultural trailer and was taken on journeys into remote areas. Its later history included use by successive generations of the Falconer family. The car's long ownership history is unusually well documented. Contemporary newspaper records from 1924 record its registration to the Falconer family, while later specialist histories trace its use and ownership through subsequent generations.Its original body survived decades of hard useDuring the Depression, the Falconers adapted the Barker body to function partly as a utility vehicle, increasing the space available for carrying equipment and goods. The alteration was carried out without destroying the original Barker coachwork. The rear doors remained with the car, while their handles and the rear top bows were retained separately.The car continued to be used for decades. Family photographs and historical records document the Silver Ghost working in Western Australia during the 1940s and 1950s, including journeys into the Kimberley region. The original engine and gearbox remained with the car despite this extensive use. The Silver Ghost later appeared at Rolls-Royce Owners Club events, including the 1997 Federal Rally in Perth, where it reportedly covered about 400 kilometres during the event.The 2026 auction ended without a saleGooding Christie’s offered chassis 17CB as Lot 40 at its 2026 Amelia Island Auctions with an estimate of $350,000 to $450,000. The listing presented it as an unusually preserved pre-war Silver Ghost with original Barker coachwork, original mechanical components and approximately 100 years of Falconer family ownership. The car was not sold at the auction. Its appearance at Amelia Island therefore did not result in a public sale price, but it brought the history of a particularly unusual Australian Silver Ghost back into the collector-car market.Chassis 17CB should also not be confused with another 1915 Silver Ghost, chassis 24CB. That separate car is fitted with engine 15A and original Maythorn & Son coachwork, confirming that the two chassis numbers refer to different cars. For 17CB, the defining story remains its own: a 1915 Silver Ghost with original Barker coachwork that arrived in Australia during the First World War, passed to the Falconer family in 1924, remained with them for roughly a century and eventually emerged from long-term storage to appear at auction in 2026.You use AI every day. articles.title: Dangers unseen: Unprotected and unlit, Delhi parks fail safety tests after dark
articles.summary: A well-lit pathway can give way to darkness within a few turns. A guarded entrance at one end may be undone by an unmanned gate at another.
articles.body: A well-lit pathway can give way to darkness within a few turns. A guarded entrance at one end may be undone by an unmanned gate at another. Across some of Delhi’s sprawling parks, lighting, visibility and security change sharply from one stretch to the next, leaving secluded pockets within otherwise busy public spaces.The conditions assume significance after the alleged gang rape of a minor at Aastha Kunj Park brought safety inside the capital’s green spaces into focus. TOI visits some of them.MAZE OF UNLIT TRAILSAt Buddha Jayanti Park in Central Ridge, a few steps are enough to move from a manicured pathway into a maze of overgrown tracks. Gate No. 2 was still open at 6pm. Cars could drive into the parking area, but there was no guard stationed at the entrance. From there, a lane on the left stretched towards the canteen. This was groomed, easy to follow and lined with lamp posts, though the lights had not been switched on as the park neared its closing time.But take the tracks to the right, and the setting changes abruptly. Narrow trails disappeared into thick, unkempt vegetation, some seemingly running endlessly into the bushes. At places, shrubs hung so low over the tracks that one had to stoop to pass. Unlike the peripheral path, where lamp posts stood roughly 50 metres apart, several of these inner tracks had no visible lighting at all. There were few people around: a family of three, a few couples and a biker. “I have a field job and there is no entry fee here, so I came to the park to rest,” the biker said.According to the timings displayed on a board, the park remains open from 5am to 7pm between April 1 and Sept 30, and 6am to 6pm from Oct 1 to March 31. At 6.15pm, toilets were being locked, and people were asked to leave the park. Yet, with the entrance unguarded and several secluded tracks cutting through the vegetation, monitoring who remained inside appeared to rest largely on a final sweep of the grounds.A guard in civilian clothes, carrying a stick, was seen telling visitors to leave. “I check the whole park to make sure everyone has left. Then I lock it,” he said. “Four people are there to look after it, but the others have gone to their villages. So, I am the only one here. I have already locked one gate at 6pm. Now I have to lock the other.”In 2003, a 17-year-old DU student was raped by two members of the President’s Bodyguard inside this park. Four personnel were ultimately convicted. In 2010, two drivers associated with Delhi Police were arrested for allegedly attempting to rape a woman and assaulting her companion inside the park.WHEN PHONE FLASHLIGHT IS A MUSTThe phone flashlight comes out before the evening walk is over. At several points inside Rohini’s Swarn Jayanti Park, visitors use it to find their way through the darkness. For a park’s safety check, it’s an immediate red flag. Spread across 170 acres, Japanese Park, as it is popularly known, has gardens, boating areas and picnic spots. The crowds and lights at the entrance can make it feel alive. However, the deeper one goes, the harder it is to spot a guard or even another visitor.In 2013, a businessman’s body with his throat slit was found in a lake inside the park, after which the park was reportedly shut before reopening in 2015. In 2017, two 19-year-old cousins were chased and stabbed to death inside the park. In Jan 2026, an 18-year-old was stabbed to death.A recent spot check found a guard at Gate 1 near the parking area, but little security was visible inside. At several points, visitors used phone flashlights to walk. The closing time appeared another grey area. Some said it is 7.30pm, others 8pm. Yet people remained inside beyond these timings. Google lists it as open till 11pm. Given the park’s size and dense stretches, someone venturing too deep could even struggle to find his way back. Tushali, a resident from a nearby area, said she avoids going deep after dark. Sima, a regular visitor, said she knows which areas to avoid and claimed couples, gamblers and smokers gather deeper inside. Anushka, visiting with her husband, said she felt fine when accompanied but found the isolated stretches uncomfortable when alone.TRESPASSERS FOX GUARDSAt Vijay Mandal Park in Begumpur, a short walk from Sri Aurobindo College, the evening deadline appeared to mark the end of official access, but not necessarily of movement into the park. The green space, frequented by walkers and college students during the day, was dimly lit as darkness set in. Lamp posts were there, but dark pockets still existed as some people walked and jogged around. One woman had her phone flashlight on. A board at the entrance listed the park’s timings as 5am to 8pm.At 8pm, two guards shut the main gate, stopping people from entering and asking those inside to leave. Yet, two people could be seen scaling the iron grille along the park’s boundary and jumping inside at that very moment.A guard stationed at the entrance said there is another gate on the opposite side of the park. “But we aren’t sure if that gate is still open or whether the guards on that side will man it after 8pm,” he said. Some students said poor lighting added to their unease. “Trespassers are common. For women, it’s not safe. There should be more lighting,” said Manish, a second-year Sri Aurobindo College student. Himani, another second-year student, said she avoids the park after sunset. Some visitors alleged that people entered the park just to consume drugs.A Congress worker was beaten and shot dead while taking a morning walk in this park last year, while in 2023, a woman was hit with an iron rod and killed in broad daylight.NEITHER BLEAK NOR PERFECTSheesh Mahal Park in Shalimar Bagh presents a mixed picture. The DDAmanaged park is mostly well lit with guard rooms at several points. But its quiet, secluded stretches have witnessed serious crime.In 2017, a 16-year-old girl was gang-raped inside the park, while her male friend was assaulted and robbed. The case exposed the park’s dark patches at that time — from faulty high-mast lights, broken boundary walls (now, there’s a grille) and a shortage of guards. In Aug 2023, a labourer was found dead inside the park, with police registering a case of murder.At the entrance, a board called it a “family park” and warned against “indecent activities”. As the sun set and the crowd thinned, much of the park remained lit. But deep inside, several lights were not working, and dark patches appeared here and there. Urmila, returning from work, said she avoids the quieter stretches because the lights are often on the blink.Dinesh Sharma, who was with his daughter, said things were different three to four years ago, when gamblers used to frequent the park. Since exArmy personnel became guards, things are “way better”, he claimed.TOI found seven to eight guards stationed at one point, who said they patrol the park. Still, the dark stretches remained. For visitors, the equation is simple: guards help, but a faulty light or two can still turn a lush patch into a blind spot.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Words long used in Caribbean, Bermuda are now part of Oxford dictionary
articles.summary: SAN JUAN (PUERTO RICO): More than a dozen words long used in Bermuda and across the Caribbean got an official nod on Wednesday from the Oxford English
articles.body: SAN JUAN (PUERTO RICO): More than a dozen words long used in Bermuda and across the Caribbean got an official nod on Wednesday from the Oxford English Dictionary. First in line is “bimpert,” a Bermudian word of unknown origin that is used to describe a stupid or foolish person. People on the tiny island in the north Atlantic often use it in this traditional phrase: “A bimpert is justah wuffless bye,” which roughly translates to: an idiot is just a worthless boy.Another colourful addition is “hornerman,” a word used in the eastern Caribbean island of Trinidad and Tobago since 1975 to describe an unfaithful man or a man having a relationship with someone else's partner.If someone in the Caribbean were to find out about such infidelities, they might be known “to get on,” which means to have an emotional outburst or make a scene, or “to cut someone’s tail,” meaning to beat someone.Depending on the fallout from such infidelities, a woman might need “vex money,” which refers to “money carried or kept in a safe place by a woman, for use in an emergency or in any unexpected eventuality.”Among other dark words that made the list is “jablesse,” defined as "a malevolent shape-shifting female spirit with one cloven hoof, which at night is said to assume the form of a beautiful woman to lure men to their deaths.” It is derived from “diablesse,” the French word for female demon.Another supernatural entry is “douen." It is “typically depicted as short in stature, with backward-pointing feet, and wearing a large hat, said to be the spirit of a child who died before it could be baptized, and believed to lure children into the forest by calling their names,” according to the dictionary. It is a variation of the Spanish word “duende,” which means elf.Several food-related words were included this year: “shadeesh,” the Bermudian word for chorizo; “sugar cake,” made of grated coconut boiled with sugar, water and spices; and “peanut punch,” a wildly popular rich and frothy beverage made with peanuts, milk, sugar and several spices.In the Caribbean, one might sit down to have a peanut punch with one’s “nana” or “nani,” which are used to address one’s maternal grandparents. In Bermuda, one would sit down to partake with a “hamma,” or friend. The final Caribbean English words added this year are “Trinbagonian,” which refers to people from both the islands of Trinidad and Tobago, and “canboulay,” which refers to Carnival festivities in Trinidad in the 1800s that celebrated the emancipation of slaves. They stem from a 1700s harvest festival that British tried to quash, leading to riots re-enacted to this day to mark the start of Carnival. Canboulay is derived from “burning cane,” which the dictionary noted was associated with “acts of defiance”.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Alex Trebek’s former LA home was demolished after his death; a new 20,000-square-foot mansion replaced the house his family lived in for nearly 30 years
articles.summary: For almost three decades, the Studio City property was closely tied to Alex Trebek’s family life.
articles.body: For almost three decades, the Studio City property was closely tied to Alex Trebek’s family life. Trebek bought the California house in 1991, not long after marrying Jean, and spent years changing, repairing and maintaining it himself. It was where the couple raised their children and where Trebek continued his interest in construction away from the Jeopardy! studio. After he died in 2020, the house was put on the market and sold in 2022. A year later, photographs showed the old building being reduced to rubble. The property itself did not disappear, though. As reported by The Sun, the 1.5-acre site has since been redeveloped, with a far larger modern farmhouse-style mansion taking the place of the house Trebek and his family had known for so long.Alex Trebek bought the Studio City home for $2.15 million in 1991The house stood on Fryman Road in Studio City, on a 1.5-acre parcel in Fryman Estates. Trebek bought it for $2.15 million in 1991 and lived there with Jean for nearly 30 years. The original property dated to 1923 and had a Mediterranean-style appearance, with the scale and layout of a substantial family residence rather than a newly built modern compound.By the time the house was offered for sale in January 2022, it had about 10,000 square feet of living space. There were five bedrooms and nine bathrooms, along with a two-storey entrance, dual staircases, a library, media room and cinema. Outside, the grounds included a guesthouse, gardens, a fountain and a swimming pool with a slide.The sale came not long after Trebek's death. His daughter Emily, a Los Angeles-based estate agent, helped put the property on the market with an asking price of $7 million. It eventually sold for $6.45 million in May 2022, as reported by The Sun.The Studio City house became a project for Trebek over the yearsThe property was more than a place Trebek happened to live. He was heavily involved in its upkeep and renovation, an interest that went back much further than his television career.In 2019, he undertook a major renovation of the couple's primary bathroom as a gift to Jean. He later described the difficulties of working on an older house, including problems that only became apparent once demolition had begun. The finished bathroom was something he was particularly pleased with because, as he put it, Jean liked the result.That interest in houses had been with him since childhood. Trebek said he had once wanted to become an architect and later considered getting into real estate, even planning to work on his first house renovation with his father. Home improvement remained a personal interest throughout his years on television.Photographs of the property before its demolition showed how much of that character had accumulated over the years. Books were visible around the house, while the kitchen opened into the main living areas. The cinema, formal entrance and pool area gave the property the scale expected of a high-end Los Angeles residence, but the renovation work gave it a more personal connection to its owner.The house stood for decades before demolition began in 2023By September 2023, the long-time Trebek residence was being dismantled. Photos shared online showed construction machinery working through the building, bringing down a property that had stood on the site for decades.Reports at the time said demolition permits had been issued earlier that year. The new owners had acquired the property after its 2022 sale, and the old house was subsequently cleared from the site.The timing made the demolition particularly striking for people familiar with Trebek's connection to the house. He died in November 2020, and the property had only changed hands in 2022. By the following year, the rooms associated with his family life, his renovations and his years away from the Jeopardy! set were gone.Some fans reacted to photographs of the demolition on Reddit and a Jeopardy! discussion forum. Several remembered Trebek talking about repairing the house himself, while others recalled stories connected with the property.A new 20,000-square-foot mansion replaced Trebek’s former homeThe demolition did not leave the 1.5-acre property vacant for long. Later reporting shows that developers Mark Alexander and Rob Diaz acquired the site and built a new residence in its place.Mansion Global reported in September 2025 that the replacement was a modern farmhouse-style mansion of around 20,000 square feet, making it roughly twice the size of the 10,000-square-foot Trebek residence that previously stood there. The report said the property was being offered for $42 million.The new building has a very different architectural language. Rather than reproducing the old Mediterranean-style house, the developers created a contemporary compound with two large A-frame forms around the entrance, cedar-clad exterior walls and sloping slate roofs.The property remains heavily landscaped despite the scale of the new construction. The new residence was designed around a courtyard and swimming pool, with additional limestone structures containing wellness and gym facilities. The grounds were planted with mature trees and thousands of native plants, according to Mansion Global.From a 10,000-square-foot family home to a modern compoundTrebek's former house covered about 10,000 square feet and contained five bedrooms and nine bathrooms. The replacement has been described as approximately 20,000 square feet, with eight bedrooms in the Mansion Global report.The transformation also changes what the address represents. For nearly 30 years, it was the Trebek family's private home, shaped in part by the host's own repairs and renovations. The newer building belongs to a different period of the property's history, with its design conceived as a new development rather than an adaptation of the house Trebek maintained.The property’s history did not end with the demolitionTrebek's former house is therefore no longer standing, but the property itself has taken on another life. The same parcel that once held a 1923 Mediterranean-style residence now contains a contemporary mansion several times larger in scale and designed for a very different purpose.The change happened in stages: Trebek bought the property for $2.15 million in 1991, lived there with his family for almost three decades, and spent years working on the house. It was listed after his death, sold for $6.45 million in 2022 and demolished in 2023. The redevelopment that followed eventually produced a modern mansion reported at around 20,000 square feet.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: 'Obviously unacceptable': Australia accuses OpenAI of breaching government website
articles.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese on Wednesday said that an artificial intelligence agent developed by OpenAI hacked into Australia's national
articles.body: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese on Wednesday said that an artificial intelligence agent developed by OpenAI hacked into Australia's national healthcare database in June, gaining access to both public and non-public files of the country's Medicare statistics database.Albanese said that OpenAI notified the government earlier this month using an email sent to a “public mailbox”.“Today, I spoke with the CEO of OpenAI, Sam Altman, to express Australia’s extreme concern about this incident and I also expressed my disappointment that it took the company way too long to inform the government what had occurred," Albanese said on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.He said that a probe is under way to ascertain what other government systems were affected.“A forensic investigation aided by the Australian signals directorate is now under way to ascertain more information, including what other government systems were affected,” Australian PM said.“Evidence currently available is that there is no broader compromise to the ... network. Nonetheless, this situation is obviously unacceptable,” he added.Albanese said that Australia had voiced its “extreme concern about this incident” to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, adding that he was deeply disappointed by the company's delay in notifying the government.Albanese also said that the investigation would also examine why government systems had failed to detect the breach in the first place.“The question is, when it was trying to harvest data, did it go into these other sites? So we're not confirming that that occurred,” he said.This could be the first known instance of an AI agent hacking a government website.What OpenAI saidMeanwhile, OpenAI, in a statement, said that its review found no evidence of patient records being accessed.“Our review found no evidence of patient records being accessed. The information accessed included aggregate health statistics and internal file names,” it said.It added that it “identified activity involving several Australian government websites and services as our models attempted to look up answers. Our models took actions we did not intend.”The Australian breach is the latest of several recent incidents in which OpenAI has disclosed hacks or unauthorised activity involving its AI agents well after they occurred.In some cases, this was because the activity was only detected belatedly, and in others because the company initially elected not to disclose it.A separate high-profile incident, a mid-July intrusion into open-source AI repository Hugging Face, was only detected about a week after it took place, according to timelines released by OpenAI and independent investigators.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2024, a 57-year-old man ran from Cape Town to Cairo in 301 days; gunmen in Ethiopia nearly kidnapped him during his 6,706-mile long journey
articles.summary: Keith Boyd completed a 6,706-mile journey from Cape Town to Cairo in 301 days in 2024, setting a new record for the fastest journey between the two cities
articles.body: Keith Boyd completed a 6,706-mile journey from Cape Town to Cairo in 301 days in 2024, setting a new record for the fastest journey between the two cities on foot. The 57-year-old British-South African runner crossed 9 countries during the challenge, but the route became particularly dangerous in Ethiopia, where he and his videographer were stopped, beaten and held by armed men. Despite the serious security problems, Boyd eventually completed the remaining section of his route and reached Cairo, surpassing the previous record by 17 days.How did a 57-year-old run from Cape Town to CairoBoyd covered 10,793 kilometres, travelling through South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Tanzania, Kenya, Ethiopia, Sudan and Egypt. Guinness World Records reported that he completed the journey in 301 days, beating a 25-year-old record of 318 days by 17 days. Men's Fitness reported his exact finishing time as 301 days, 20 hours and 58 minutes, with Boyd reaching Cairo on 22 May 2024.The route was not simply a continuous run from one capital to another. Boyd had to change his plans because of the conflict in Sudan. He had originally intended to travel in the opposite direction, from Cairo to Cape Town, but chose to begin in South Africa in the hope that conditions in Sudan would improve by the time he reached that country.The journey was supported by a small team travelling in a van carrying camping equipment and medical supplies. During the earlier stages, Boyd made steady progress. Guinness World Records reported that he crossed South Africa in 47 days, while Botswana and Zimbabwe took a little over two weeks. Zambia, Tanzania and Kenya each took roughly a month.The daily running routine behind Boyd’s record-breaking journeyBoyd averaged around 50 kilometres a day during much of the challenge, often dividing the distance into five 10-kilometre sections. As reported by Men's Fitness, he described a slightly different routine during the Sudan and Egypt sections, when he normally began around 5.30am and ran four blocks of about 12.5 kilometres, walking for 20 to 30 minutes between them.Not every day followed the same pattern. Some days involved as little as 5 kilometres, while others reached 50 kilometres. Overall, Men's Fitness reported 125 days as his longest continuous stretch of back-to-back running. It also reported 60 non-running days, including 54 linked to Ethiopian security and paperwork problems, five because of illness and one for repacking.Preparation for such a long journey was intensive. Guinness World Records reported that Boyd trained for 4 months, running about 200 kilometres each week to build strength and endurance in his feet, legs and back.How did the Ethiopia kidnapping attempt change the journeyEthiopia became the most dangerous part of the expedition. Boyd was travelling through the northern Amhara region when he and his videographer were stopped by armed men. According to Guinness World Records, the pair were beaten and forced into a van after being intercepted while trying to cross the area.Men's Fitness reported that the gunmen demanded his support team to arrange for a ransom. He and the videographer were threatened with being taken into a forest, where finding them would have been extremely difficult. Boyd managed to delay the situation and eventually negotiated their release for $1,000.Afterwards, he continued for another 100 kilometres with a military escort. The security situation eventually became too dangerous, however, and he had to leave Ethiopia and continue towards Sudan without completing that section.The experience meant that reaching Cairo did not immediately mark the end of the challenge. Boyd still had approximately 500 kilometres of Ethiopia to complete.The final Ethiopian section brought further dangerAfter reaching Cairo, Boyd sought permission and security assistance to return to Ethiopia and finish the missing section. Guinness World Records reported that he petitioned the Ethiopian government for protection but received no response for almost three weeks. He eventually arranged the journey with local civilians and officials.The return was still extremely difficult. Guinness World Records reported that Boyd and his team were ambushed and had to take cover in a ditch. They were also held overnight in an overcrowded cell without being charged and faced further threats and assaults from armed men. Despite those setbacks, he completed the final stretch and left the region safely.Why did Boyd take on such a demanding challengeThe run had a purpose beyond the record. Guinness World Records reported that Boyd undertook the challenge to raise money for Rainbow Leaders, his non-profit organisation, which works to encourage young people in Africa to participate in elections as part of efforts to address poverty.Boyd had also spent more than 30 years working in telecommunications in Africa, giving him a long personal connection with the continent and its communities. The challenge therefore combined an endurance goal with fundraising and civic engagement.The run took a heavy physical tollThe distance and length of the journey placed considerable strain on Boyd's body. Men's Fitness reported that his feet and particularly his left ankle became swollen, while he also developed tendonitis. He used 3 types of running shoes to deal with different problems, including ankle stability, impact and rough terrain.Recovery became part of his daily routine. Boyd said he aimed for 8 to 9 hours of sleep and used stretching and a roller to help his body recover. He also consumed protein through shakes and bars, although he lost weight and muscle from his thighs during the journey.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on the US and China to be “partners, not rivals” as he arrived in Washington on Wednesday for a state visit.
articles.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on the US and China to be “partners, not rivals” as he arrived in Washington on Wednesday for a state visit.In his written arrival statement at Joint Base Andrews, Xi said the two countries’ interests are “deeply intertwined” and that China’s “great rejuvenation” and US President Donald Trump’s goal of “making America great again” can go hand in hand.Xi, in his arrival statement, said the two countries should work towards a stable relationship with cooperation as the main focus, measured competition and controllable differences.He also said he looked forward to discussing major issues with Trump and expanding exchanges and cooperation between the two countries.Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan were received at Joint Base Andrews by Trump and First Lady Melania Trump.Xi is in the US from September 23 to 25 at Trump’s invitation. The White House said Trump and Melania will host a formal state arrival ceremony for Xi and Peng at the White House on Thursday, followed by a state dinner in the evening.The White House said the formal ceremony will involve 479 military personnel from all branches of the US armed forces, military demonstrations and a flypast featuring a B-2 Spirit and four F-22 Raptors. articles.title: In 1998, David Mason walked 5,500 km across Australia with three camels; 236 days later, he reached the coast and won Adventurer of the Year
articles.summary: In 1998, David Mason became the first person to walk solo across the Australian continent, completing an eight-month, 5,500-kilometre journey accompanied
articles.body: In 1998, David Mason became the first person to walk solo across the Australian continent, completing an eight-month, 5,500-kilometre journey accompanied by three camels. The 236-day trek later earned him the 1999 Australian Geographic Adventurer of the Year award. Seventeen years on, Mason flew to Broome for an emotional reunion with Kabul, the last surviving camel from his historic crossing. Here's the story behind Mason's journey, and what became of him and his camel afterwards.David Mason's 1998 solo crossing of Australia with three camelsMason began his 1998 crossing alone, and later picked up three camels at Dalby to carry his supplies during the journey across Australia's desert regions. The journey covered roughly 5,500 kilometres and took eight months, or 236 days, to complete. Mason said the experience gave him a sense of owning his own days and future that he couldn't find anywhere else, comparing it to the sacrifices and rewards faced by a single-handed yachtsman attempting a solo ocean crossing.The idea's origin: French Foreign Legion in AfricaThe trip's origins trace back to Mason's time serving with the French Foreign Legion in Africa. "I was a foreign legionnaire, and I was sitting on top of a hill looking over Ethiopia, thinking there's got to be a heck of a lot more to life than this," he told ABC News. "I thought, why not catch some camels and walk across Australia? It was pretty much as simple as that." What began as a fairly spontaneous idea eventually turned into months of preparation before Mason and his three camels hit the road, and the story has since been recorded in two books.Kabul, the lead camel and the emotional 2015 reunionOf the three camels who accompanied Mason, Kabul, his lead camel, proved an especially invaluable companion through cold nights, hot days and seemingly endless roads. "He was, and is, phlegmatic, powerful and utterly trustworthy, and without him I couldn't have done the trip," Mason said. After the walk, the camels joined the camel trains on Cable Beach in Broome. In 2015, 17 years after the crossing, Mason returned to Broome to reunite with Kabul, telling ABC News he began to tear up as he approached the camel, who by then was cared for by cameleer John Geappen and was living out his days on the Kimberley coast.Life after the walk: Adventurer of the Year and military serviceMason's 1998 crossing raised thousands of dollars for the Fred Hollows Foundation and earned him the 1999 Australian Geographic Adventurer of the Year award. In the years since, he has stayed far from idle, serving overseas with the Australian Defence Force, completing four tours of Iraq, and later working as a military lawyer based in Canberra. Even so, Mason said the 236 days he spent on the road with Kabul by his side have stayed with him ever since. "I think about it all the time," he said while describing an enduring sense of freedom he has continued to chase in the years that followed.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
